Platform/Brand/Method: Radio-immunoassay (RIA), in-house, using Antiserum-I ('a more specific antiserum (Antiserum-I) to digoxin (Dx)', prepared previously by the same authors — Ikeda and Fujii, 2000; Ikeda et al., 2002); [3H]-Dx tracer with dextran-coated charcoal separation
Assay generation/version: Antiserum-I (final dilution 1:2200; standard curve linear 0.1–20 ng/ml)
Direction (user APS): not reported in the information source
Interferent concentration (exact, with u: PRE 69 mg/kg/day, i.p. — three times pretreatment
Baseline analyte concentration: not reported in the information source
Final analyte concentration: not reported in the information source
Absolute change (as reported): not reported in the information source
Percentage change (as reported): not reported in the information source
Absolute change (calculated): not reported in the information source
Percentage change (calculated): not reported in the information source
Magnitude of change (verbatim from sourc: "three times pretreatment with PRE did not obviously change the serum concentrations time curve of Dx"
Clinical significance vs user APS: Not significant up to PRE 69 mg/kg/day, i.p. — three times pretreatment per study; user APS 3% (no quantitative magnitude reported)
Sample type: Rat serum (Wistar male rats, 9–10 weeks, 282±16 g; serum separated by centrifugation 1600×g, 10 min)
Study method details: In vivo drug–drug interaction study, not a CLSI EP7-type analytical interference protocol: 'rats were pretreated with PRE (69 mg/kg/day, i.p.) for 3, 6, and 9 days' (p.1058) — the PDF names a corn oil vehicle for DEX and for the control injections but does not state the PRE vehicle; PRE supplied by Wako Pure Chemical Industries (Osaka, Japan) (p.1057, §Materials); Dx 0.017 mg/kg (250 µl of 5% ethanol solution) injected via the femoral vein 1.5 hour after the last PRE treatment; blood withdrawn from the carotid vein; serum Dx measured by RIA; AUC0→8 and MRT calculated by the trapezoidal rule; CLtot = Di.v./AUC0→8,i.v.; Vdss = CLtot×MRTi.v.; n = 5 rats per group; corn oil-untreated rats used as control (corn oil-treated vs untreated not significantly different, data not shown)
Additional sources of bias: Rat serum, not human serum; deliberately high glucocorticoid dose — 'we selected the high dose treatment of glucocorticoids' (p.1064); n = 5 rats per group; the authors state 'the use of rat as a model to predict or explain the drug interaction of Dx in human is not appropriate' (p.1065); the effect is pharmacokinetic (CYP3A2/P-glycoprotein induction) rather than analytical, since PRE cross-reactivity is <0.05% (p.1058); no oral-administration or Cmax data are reported for PRE-pretreated rats
Notes: Comparator/pool: control rats (corn oil-untreated), Antiserum-I, Fig. 3B. Serum Dx concentration-time course reported graphically on a logarithmic axis; individual time-point concentrations are neither printed nor data-labelled, so baseline, final and both calculated change columns are the missing literal (no interpolation from the plot). 'Direction (user APS)' is the missing literal because no quantitative magnitude of change is reported for this figure. Appraisal anchors: 'Physiologically realistic concentration?' = Borderline because the PDF confirms the two drugs are genuinely co-prescribed — 'Dx and PRE are co-administered for the treatment of systemic lupus erythematosus with interstitial myocarditis (Takahashi et al., 1999)' (p.1057) — but the dose used here was chosen to be supra-therapeutic: 'we selected the high dose treatment of glucocorticoids' (p.1064). 'Real-world conditions reflected?' = Partial for the same reason (real co-administration, native circulating Dx and metabolites, but rat model and a high dose).
